briefs.heading: Where should the reports API keep its cache?
briefs.why_now: the reports API ships next week; until you answer, it ships with no cache
context: The reports API reads the same few rows many times a second at the busy hour.
A cache saves those reads, and where it lives decides what it costs to run.
terms: the share of reads the cache answers without asking the database
briefs.recommend: the hit rate is still a guess, and the in-process cache needs no new service

options.leads_to: each server keeps its own copy, so there is nothing new to run
options.choose_if: running fewer services matters more than the highest hit rate
options.downside: each server warms up alone, so a restart sends a burst of reads to the database

options.leads_to: all servers read one copy, so the hit rate is higher
options.choose_if: the highest hit rate matters more than one more service to run
options.downside: one more service to run, and every read crosses the network

checked.text: `reports.log` shows 120 requests per second at the busy hour

briefs.not_checked: the real hit rate, which a week of trial traffic would show

undo.text: switch the cache flag back and redeploy
